title: R bookmark restore value shape differs from Python
description:
R's bookmark restore serializer uses `jsonlite::toJSON(auto_unbox = TRUE)`, so a length-1 R vector (e.g. a checkbox-group with one selected value) serializes as a JSON scalar `"a"`, whereas Python `json.dumps` emits `["a"]`. This can seed the wrong shape into the JS input registry for single-value multi-value inputs on restore. Needs a cross-language bookmark-payload fixture and a shape-preserving fix (hard due to R's lack of a scalar vs. vector distinction).

Note: re-verify against current code; the broad bookmarking issue #27 is closed.

_Filed from the retired `docs/todos.md`._

title: useShinyOutputValue() returns null but is typed T | undefined
description:
`useShinyOutputValue()` returns `null` when the server sends `NULL`, but it is typed `T | undefined`. Code that narrows with `!== undefined` type-checks, then crashes at runtime.

```r
# app.R
library(shiny)
library(shinyreact)

shinyApp(page_react(), function(input, output, session) {
  output$x <- reactive_output(NULL)
})
```

```tsx
const x = useShinyOutputValue<{ n: number }>("x"); // typed { n: number } | undefined
if (x !== undefined) x.n; // TypeError: Cannot read properties of null
```

Returning `NULL` until inputs arrive is the pattern the docs recommend, so this is the common case. The return type should include `null`.

Related: the `@posit-dev/shinyreact/styles` export has no `.css` suffix, so TypeScript can't resolve `import "@posit-dev/shinyreact/styles"` without a `declare module`.

shinyreact 0.1.0 (CRAN) / `@posit-dev/shinyreact` 0.1.1, shiny 1.14.0.

title: page_react() drops a dependency when the app folder shares its name
description:
`page_react()` names the app's own dependency (the one that loads `www/ui.js`) after the app folder. Shiny keeps one dependency per name, so when the folder has the same name as another dependency on the page, one of the two never loads. Nothing warns about it.

I ran into this while hosting a reactable through `ShinyOutput`, the setup from #317. My app folder was called `react/`, and reactR ships React as a dependency named `react`. The browser never got React, and reactable failed with:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'useLayoutEffect')
    at reactable-binding-0.4.5/reactable.js
```

Renaming the folder fixed it, but it took me a while to connect that error to the folder name.

## Reproduce

Two files in a folder named `react/`:

`app.R`

```r
library(shiny)
library(shinyreact)

ui <- page_react()

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$tbl <- reactable::renderReactable(reactable::reactable(mtcars))
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

`www/ui.js`

```js
const { React, ReactDOM, ShinyOutput } = window.shinyreact;
const h = React.createElement;

ReactDOM.createRoot(document.body.appendChild(document.createElement("div"))).render(
  h(ShinyOutput, { id: "tbl", className: "reactable html-widget html-widget-output" }),
);
```

The table stays empty and the console shows the error above. The page loads `react-1791721216/ui.js` but never reactR's `react-18.2.0/react.min.js` or `react-dom.min.js`. Copy the same two files into a folder named `tables/` and the table renders with no errors.

A folder named `shinyreact/` breaks the app by itself, in both R and Python (a bare `page_react()` app whose `ui.js` reads `window.shinyreact`). The page loads the app's `ui.js` and skips `shinyreact.js`, so the first line of `ui.js` fails:

```
TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'React' of 'window.shinyreact' as it is undefined.
```

## Cause

In both R and Python, `page_react()` passes the folder name to `page_react_dep()` as the dependency name. The version is the modified time of `ui.js`, so a big number like `1791721216`. What happens next depends on when the other dependency shows up:

- On the first page, htmltools keeps the highest version of each name. The app's version beats any real one, so the other package loses. That's the `shinyreact/` case.
- Dependencies that arrive later, like the ones `renderReactable()` brings, go through `renderDependency()` in shiny.js, which skips any name it has already seen. That's the `react/` case.

## Suggestion

Give the app's dependency a name no package will use, like `shinyreact-app-<folder>`, or just `shinyreact-app`, which `page_react()` already falls back to when it can't get a folder name. There's only one per page, and only the URL of `ui.js` would change. The page title can keep using the folder name.

A warning when the folder name matches another dependency would help less: when the page is built, it can't see dependencies that arrive later, like reactable's, so it would miss the case I hit.

## Versions

- R: shinyreact 0.1.0 (GitHub 0ff27a2, and `page_react()` is the same on main), shiny 1.14.0, htmltools 0.5.9, reactable 0.4.5, reactR 0.6.1
- Python: shinyreact 0.1.0, shiny 1.8.0

title: feat(skills): Add `skill` function
description:
## `skill()` function vs. installed skills (library-skills / btw) Someone asked for a `skill("SKILLNAME")` function in shinyreact that prints the requested skill. mirai, posit-dev/py-shiny and rstudio/shiny already do it another way: they ship skills inside the package (`inst/skills/`, `.agents/skills/`), and a separate tool (btw for R, library-skills for Python) installs or discovers them. shinyreact already ships both copies (`pkg-r/inst/skills/`, `pkg-py/src/shinyreact/.agents/skills/`), so this is a question of how agents *reach* the content. Writing the content is already done. 🟢 pro · 🔴 con · 🟡 depends / partial | Theme | `skill()` function | library-skills / btw install | |---|---|---| | **Discovery** | 🔴 The agent must already know the function exists. Nothing in context triggers it unless a README, docs or btw tool listing points to it.
🟢 Shows up in the exported function list and help index. | 🟢 The `description` frontmatter sits in context, so the agent triggers the skill automatically when it's relevant. This is the main reason skills exist. | | **Freshness / version match** | 🟢 Always matches the package version loaded in this session, including inside renv or a venv. | 🟡 Matches the installed package if the tool reads from or symlinks to the package path. Goes stale if the tool copies files (verify per tool).
🔴 A global install can describe a different version than the project's renv or venv uses. | | **Harness compatibility** | 🟢 Works anywhere the agent can run R or Python: Positron Assistant, Cursor, an MCP `run_r_code` tool, ChatGPT with code execution. | 🔴 Only works in harnesses that understand skills.
🟢 Uses the standard skill layout agents already know, so it keeps working as the standard evolves. | | **Permissions / runtime** | 🔴 Needs code-execution permission, which many harnesses gate behind approval.
🔴 Needs a live session with shinyreact installed, and R/Python startup costs seconds per call.
🔴 Can't help before shinyreact is installed ("should I use this?"). | 🟢 Plain file reads: works offline, in read-only mode and in plan mode. | | **Context cost** | 🟢 Costs nothing until the function is called. | 🟡 Only the frontmatter is loaded until a skill triggers. Small per skill, but it grows with every package that ships skills. | | **Depth (references, scripts, assets)** | 🔴 Everything comes out as one print. Extra content needs a second call (`skill("create-app", "npm")`) or printed absolute paths for the agent to read.
🔴 Skill scripts and assets can't be used from printed text. | 🟢 Reference files are read only when needed. Scripts and assets work as-is. | | **Dynamic content** | 🟢 Can be generated at runtime: installed version, whether `node`/`npm` exist, shipped examples via `system.file()`, the current project's `www/`. | 🔴 Static Markdown. | | **Output fidelity** | 🔴 Stdout is lossy: tool-output truncation, console-width wrapping, ANSI codes, encoding. | 🟢 The agent reads the Markdown file directly. | | **API surface / maintenance** | 🔴 An exported function is public API. In R it's a CRAN-facing commitment with lifecycle and deprecation rules, and in both languages it adds autocomplete noise.
🔴 **Every** package with skills would need to export its own copy of this function.
🟢 Easy to unit test, like any function. | 🟢 Keeps AI-specific helpers out of the package's API.
🔴 Two shipped copies to keep in sync (already handled by `make update-skills` and drift tests). | | **Ecosystem consistency** | 🔴 A fourth convention, different from what mirai, shiny and py-shiny do. | 🟢 One convention, so improvements to btw or library-skills reach every package at once. | | **Installation / user friction** | 🟢 Nothing to install beyond shinyreact. | 🔴 Needs a third-party tool, and R and Python use different tools and directories.
🔴 Possible skill-name collisions across packages (verify how the tools namespace names).
🟢 btw installs all skills automatically for its chat experience. | | **Project scoping / customization** | 🔴 Global to the installed package. Users can't edit or pin it. | 🟢 Can be installed per project, committed to the repo, reviewed in PRs, and customized locally. | | **Docs / human use** | 🟢 Documentation comes with it (pkgdown, quartodoc), and people can read it in the console. | 🟡 Readable as files on disk, but not part of the reference docs. | ### Options 1. **Keep the status quo:** installed skills only. 2. **Hybrid:** keep the shipped skill files as the single source and add a thin `skill()` that reads them. It would print `SKILL.md` plus the absolute paths of reference files so the agent can read them. Adds very little code and no second copy of the content. It does **not** fix discovery. 3. **`skill()` only:** drop the installed skills in favor of the function. Leaning toward **1**, and adding **2** only if someone has a concrete harness that can't load skills.

title: Publish a GitHub release with WebAssembly assets so shinylive can install shinyreact
description:
## Problem

`shinyreact` can't be used in a **shinylive** app (Quarto `{shinylive-r}` block, or
`shinylive::export()`) because there is no WebAssembly binary for it anywhere, and
the one mechanism shinylive has for GitHub-installed packages needs a release that
this repo doesn't have.

`shinylive:::get_github_wasm_assets()` handles exactly this case. When a package is
installed from GitHub, it reads `RemoteUsername` / `RemoteRepo` / `RemoteRef` from
the installed DESCRIPTION and looks for a **GitHub release tagged with that ref**,
carrying `library.data*` and `library.js.metadata` assets:

```r
tags <- gh::gh("/repos/{user}/{repo}/releases/tags/{ref}", ...)
library_data     <- Filter(\(i) grepl("library.data", i$name, fixed = TRUE), tags$assets)
library_metadata <- Filter(\(i) i$name == "library.js.metadata",             tags$assets)
```

This repo has **zero releases**, so `gh::gh()` 404s and the Quarto render aborts:

```
Error in `get_github_wasm_assets()`:
  Can't find GitHub release for github::posit-dev/shinyreact@HEAD
! Ensure a GitHub release exists for the package repository reference: "HEAD".
```

## Reproduce

```r
pak::pak("posit-dev/shinyreact/pkg-r")   # note: R package is in the pkg-r subdir
```

Then render a Quarto revealjs/html doc containing:

````
```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
library(shiny)
library(shinyreact)
# ... any shinyreact app
```
````

## Proposed fix

Build and attach WebAssembly assets on release with
<https://github.com/r-wasm/actions> (`build-rwasm` / `release-rwasm`). Two
repo-specific details:

- The R package lives in **`pkg-r/`**, not the repo root, so the action needs the
  subdirectory configured. (For the same reason, plain
  `pak::pak("posit-dev/shinyreact")` fails with *"Can't find R package in GitHub
  repo"* — it must be `posit-dev/shinyreact/pkg-r`.)
- The release tag has to match the `RemoteRef` recorded at install time. A default
  `pak::pak("posit-dev/shinyreact/pkg-r")` records `RemoteRef: HEAD`, so a release
  tagged `HEAD` is what an unpinned install looks for; a versioned tag works for
  users who install that ref explicitly.

`shinyreact` itself is pure R, so nothing needs compiling for wasm — but its
`Imports` include `brio`, which does have C code. `brio 1.1.5` is already on
repo.r-wasm.org, so a runtime install resolves it fine as long as
`https://repo.r-wasm.org` stays in the repo list.

## Things that do *not* solve this

- **Adding the package to an r-universe.** r-universe does build wasm binaries, but
  currently only for **R 4.6** (`bin/emscripten/contrib/4.6/`), and shinylive 0.10.8
  runs **R 4.5.1** (`wasm32-unknown-emscripten`). Separately, shinylive's resolver
  keys off GitHub releases, not the r-universe repo — an r-universe install has no
  `Remote*` fields, so it gets treated as CRAN-ish and is looked for on
  repo.r-wasm.org.

## Current workaround

For <https://github.com/schloerke/presentation-2026-09-15-posit-conf-shinyreact>
(a posit::conf(2026) talk), the deck ships its own single-package webR repo and
installs at runtime:

```r
webr::install(
  "shinyreact",
  repos = c("<deck>/wasm-repo", "https://repo.r-wasm.org")
)
```

with `SHINYLIVE_WASM_PACKAGES=0` set at render time purely to skip the
`get_github_wasm_assets()` lookup above. That works, but every consumer has to
rebuild and host a binary themselves. A release with wasm assets removes all of it.

title: Example: host a reactable (reactR htmlwidget) inside a shinyreact client via ShinyOutput
description:
## Motivation

#316 added a comparison article whose "Can they be combined?" section documents hosting a `reactable` inside a `ui.tsx` client through `ShinyOutput`. That was verified in a throwaway chromote spike, not shipped. An example would keep the claim honest (the repo's example tests run in each package's suite) and give people a template for the most common "I already have an R widget" case. `07-plotly` covers htmlwidgets from the plot side; reactable covers the table side and, unlike plotly, has a client→server state channel (`getReactableState()`) that needs one extra attribute to work.

## What the spike showed

- `renderReactable()` is a regular `shiny.render.function`, so shinyreact's R dep discovery loads `htmlwidgets.js`, `react-tools.js`, and `reactable.js` automatically. No manual dependency wiring.
- The `ShinyOutput` element needs the classes `reactableOutput()` emits **and** a `data-reactable-output="<id>"` attribute. Without the attribute the table renders but `getReactableState()` / `updateReactable()` never see it, because reactable reads its Shiny id from that attribute on the container's parent.
- Row selection round-trips: click a selection radio → `input$tbl__reactable__selected` → `getReactableState("tbl", "selected")` → a `reactive_output` → `useShinyOutputValue`.

Working spike (R server, no-build client):

```r
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$tbl <- reactable::renderReactable({
    reactable::reactable(head(mtcars, req(input$n)), selection = "single", onClick = "select")
  })
  output$sel <- reactive_output(reactable::getReactableState("tbl", "selected"))
}
shinyApp(page_react(), server)
```

```js
h(ShinyOutput, {
  id: "tbl",
  className: "reactable html-widget html-widget-output",
  "data-reactable-output": "tbl",
});
```

## Proposed shape

- `examples/11-reactable/` (or fold into an existing example if that reads better): `app.R`, `www/ui.js`, `FEATURES.md`, `tests/`.
- A row-count input driving the table, a `reactive_output` echoing the selected row so the client→server channel is exercised, and a `useShinyOutputStatus` dim on recalculation.
- Add to `R_EXAMPLES` in the `Makefile` and run `make update-examples` so R CMD check can reach it.
- Python side: there is no reactable for Python. Either R-only (note it in `examples/README.md`) or pair it with a Python `ShinyOutput`-hosted equivalent (`shinywidgets`? `great_tables`?) over the same `ui.js`, mirroring how `07-plotly` shares one client across both servers.
- Testing: `ui.test.ts` against the fake-Shiny harness can pin the classes and the `data-reactable-output` attribute; a testthat test can pin that `renderReactable()`'s deps are discovered. The selection round-trip is a browser claim and would wait on the R e2e suite (#194).

## Open questions

- Should `ShinyOutput` grow a documented recipe (skill or article) for "copy the attributes your `*Output()` would have emitted", since both reactable and plotly needed exactly that and it is not discoverable without reading widget source?
- Is a `shiny.react` / `shiny.fluent` example worth shipping too, or is the article section enough? It needs the manual `reactDependency()` + `shinyReactDependency()` step because `renderReact()` is not a `shiny.render.function`.

title: No way to host a real Shiny input widget (slider, native select) in a ui.tsx client
Rethink local installs: serve the npm client from .venv / renv instead of the registry
description:
Deferred question from #217, which used a repo-relative `file:../../pkg-js` as a
placeholder until the first npm publish. The placeholder works better than
expected, and that is worth taking seriously before we commit to the registry as
the only distribution channel.

## Proposal

Ship the npm-installable client (`dist-npm/`) **inside the pip wheel and the R
`inst/` directory**, and let an app install it from its own project environment:

```jsonc
// Python
{ "dependencies": { "@posit/shinyreact": "file:.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/shinyreact/npm" } }
// R (renv)
{ "dependencies": { "@posit/shinyreact": "file:renv/library/4.5/aarch64-apple-darwin20/shinyreact/npm" } }
```

`pip install shinyreact` / `install.packages("shinyreact")` would then control
**both halves** — the server and the client the browser runs — from one
dependency declaration.

## Why this isn't just Option C again

`decisions/2026-08-17-js-distribution.md` investigated and rejected Option C
("npm installs from the server package's assets"). Its disqualifier was DX:

> `file:` deps bake machine-specific absolute paths into `package.json`/lockfiles,
> breaking every collaborator, CI runner, and venv/renv rebuild

That is true of the shape it considered — `npm install "$(python -m shinyreact
npm-path)"`, which yields an absolute path. The reframing is that **modern
project environments are in-project**: uv puts the venv at `.venv/`, renv puts
the library at `renv/library/`. Both are *relative to the app directory*, so
`package.json` and the lockfile stay portable.

#217 verified this property empirically for the repo-relative case:

```
node_modules/@posit/shinyreact -> ../../../../pkg-js     # relative symlink
package-lock.json:  "resolved": "../../pkg-js", "link": true
```

Nothing machine-specific in either file.

## What it buys

- **Version skew becomes impossible by construction**, not merely loud. The
  protocol handshake (#198) stops being the thing standing between a stale
  client and a confusing bug, and goes back to being a safety net.
- **No npm release pipeline** — no `NPM_TOKEN` (#218), no three-registry release
  coordination, no "which of pip/CRAN/npm did I forget to bump".
- **Works offline / air-gapped**, and in environments where the npm registry is
  proxied or blocked.
- **The IIFE zero-build tier is untouched** — this changes only where the
  bundler tier gets its hooks from.

## What has to be answered

This is the actual work of the issue; none of these are obviously fatal, but
none are free either.

1. **Path stability.** `.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/` embeds the Python
   version; renv's library path embeds R version *and* platform. A lockfile
   pinning either breaks on an upgrade. Options: a generated stable symlink, a
   setup command that rewrites the path, or a small resolver plugin.
2. **Environments that aren't in-project.** conda, system Python, Docker layer
   caching, `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT`, `R_LIBS_USER` — all put the library
   somewhere no relative path reaches. Supported-when-in-project, documented
   otherwise? Or fall back to the registry?
3. **Tooling opacity.** A `file:`/`link:` dep is invisible to Renovate, `npm
   audit`, and npm's cache. Arguably fine — the thing under version management
   is then the pip/CRAN package — but it should be a decision, not a surprise.
4. **Ordering.** `npm install` has to run *after* `uv sync` / `renv::restore()`.
   A documented step, or a generated script?
5. **Package size.** Shipping `dist-npm/` (ESM + `.d.ts` + sourcemap) on top of
   today's `www/shinyreact.js` (205 KB) + CSS, in both the wheel and `inst/`.
6. **Does it replace npm publication, or sit beside it?** A third-party
   component library that wants to peer-depend on `@posit/shinyreact` (#32) has
   no answer except the registry. Most likely outcome: the registry stays the
   public story and this becomes the locked-version alternative — which means
   maintaining both, and that cost belongs in the decision.

## Shinylive is a non-issue

The obvious objection — "an exported app has no node, no npm, no venv layout" —
does not apply. The npm client is a **build-time** dependency: `npm install` and
`vite build` run on the developer's machine and produce `www/ui.js`.
`shinylive export` runs *afterwards* and ships that already-compiled bundle. The
toolchain and the exported runtime never meet.

If anything the npm tier is the *better* shinylive story, since with
`shinyreact_js="client"` (#217) the entire client runtime lives inside the app's
own `ui.js` rather than being resolved from a server-side `HTMLDependency` —
worth confirming as part of this work rather than assuming.

## Refs

`decisions/2026-08-17-js-distribution.md` (Options C and E), #217, #218, #172,
#32.

title: `req()`/`validate()` silent errors reach `console.error()` in ReactOutputBinding.renderError()
Two or more ShinyOutput siblings under one parent log a false "Duplicate output IDs" warning
description:
This is a preliminary finding, not a confirmed bug report. I found it while porting several Shiny apps to shinyreact's `ui.tsx` pattern, using the `shinyreact-convert-app` skill from this repo. Please check it and tell me if it makes sense.

**What I saw**

After #286 / #294, I host each real Shiny input widget with `output$<id> <- renderUI({ <the widget's own call> })` on the server, and `<ShinyOutput id="<id>" className="shiny-html-output" />` on the client. That works fine for one widget. Put two or more of these side by side under one parent element (a sidebar of several inputs, say), and the browser console logs "Duplicate output IDs were found" a few times right after the page loads, each time naming every one of those widgets. Two widgets sharing a parent: each one is reported as "2 outputs". Four widgets sharing a parent, as in a real sidebar I ported: each one is reported as "4 outputs". The count matches how many of these widgets share one parent, and stays at that number; I did not see it grow further after the page settles, even after triggering more reactive flushes with later input changes.

Minimal repro, no bslib, no theme, nothing but shinyreact:

```r
library(shiny)
library(shinyreact)

dir.create("www", showWarnings = FALSE)
writeLines(
  '(function(){
    var { React, ReactDOM, ShinyOutput, useShinyInitialized } = window.shinyreact;
    function App() {
      var ready = useShinyInitialized();
      if (!ready) return null;
      return React.createElement(
        "div",
        null,
        React.createElement(ShinyOutput, { id: "a_ui", className: "shiny-html-output" }),
        React.createElement(ShinyOutput, { id: "b_ui", className: "shiny-html-output" })
      );
    }
    var container = document.body.appendChild(document.createElement("div"));
    ReactDOM.createRoot(container).render(React.createElement(App));
  })();',
  "www/ui.js"
)

ui <- page_react(title = "dup-output-test")

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$a_ui <- renderUI(selectInput("a", "A", choices = c("x", "y")))
  output$b_ui <- renderUI(selectInput("b", "B", choices = c("x", "y")))
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Open this in a browser, and the console shows:

```
[shiny] Duplicate output IDs were found - The following IDs were used for more than one output:
- "a_ui": 2 outputs
- "b_ui": 2 outputs
```

This is not an id collision: the two ids are different strings, and `document.querySelectorAll('[id]')` shows no id used on more than one element. It is also not specific to `renderUI()`, bslib, or any theme: I removed each of those one at a time from a bigger app that showed the same warning, and the warning stayed every time.

**What I found reading the source**

`ShinyOutput`'s own mount effect (`pkg-js/src/shiny-output.tsx`) calls `Shiny.bindAll(scope)`, with `scope = el.parentElement`. That is on purpose, since `bindAll`'s own `find()` only looks at descendants. But when two or more `ShinyOutput` siblings share one parent, React fires both mount effects in the same commit, so both call `Shiny.bindAll()` on that same shared parent, close together in time.

Shiny's own `bindOutputs()` (in `shiny.js`) is `async`. For each matched element, it checks `$el.hasClass('shiny-bound-output')` first, then only adds that class after `await shinyAppBindOutput(id, bindingAdapter)` resolves. Because the class is added only after the await, both `bindAll()` calls start scanning the same parent before either await has finished. Both scans see both elements as "not yet bound", and both go ahead and bind them. Shiny's own "Duplicate output IDs" check reads a separate, module-level `bindingsRegistry`, which adds one entry every time an element gets bound and never clears it. So each element this race catches leaves one extra entry behind, even though there is really only one DOM element per id, and once that race settles on page load the reported count does not grow further; I checked this by triggering a few more reactive flushes with later input changes and saw the same numbers repeated, not higher ones.

I confirmed this by giving each `ShinyOutput` sibling its own, non-shared wrapper element (instead of two siblings directly under one parent) and nothing else changed: the warning disappeared completely.

**Does it actually break anything?**

Not that I could find so far. I checked directly, on a real app with four of these hosted inputs in one sidebar: values still arrive at the server on connect, and a server-side `updateSelectizeInput()` still drives a dependent hosted widget correctly. So today this looks like console noise and a piece of internal bookkeeping that never gets cleared, not a functional break, but I have not checked every case (a widget that gets removed and re-added later, for instance).

**One more thing I noticed**

The dynamic-input end to end test that closed #286
(`pkg-py/tests/playwright/apps/dynamic_input/app.py`) hosts both its widgets in one `renderUI()` output, one `TagList()` holding both, rather than two separate `renderUI()` outputs side by side. That sidesteps this exact case (only one `ShinyOutput` there, no siblings sharing a parent), so I don't think the test suite has caught this yet.

**What I'm asking**

Does this match what you'd expect from reading `bindOutputs()`, or is there something about it I'm missing? A fix could live in `bindOutputs()` itself (marking an element bound before starting its async work, not after) or in `ShinyOutput` (avoiding overlapping `bindAll()` calls on the same scope in the first place). I tried the second one, entirely inside `shiny-output.tsx`, and it fixed this in a real browser without changing any other observable behavior I could find. I'm opening a pull request with it right after this issue, in case it's useful, but please check whether it makes sense before merging anything.

title: Proposing two small check scripts for comparing a Shiny app to its shinyreact conversion
description:
This is a preliminary proposal, not a bug report. While porting several Shiny apps to shinyreact's `ui.tsx` pattern, using the `shinyreact-convert-app` skill from this repo, I wrote two small R scripts that caught real problems fast. I'm not attaching a PR yet, just asking whether something like this would be a welcome contribution before I spend more time cleaning them up for one. Both of the issues I opened earlier (#285, #286) were found with these.

Source (secret gist, not indexed, but the link works for anyone): https://gist.github.com/samuelbharti/aca813dedd0b8a674866b5884f1b061d

**`deps-diff.R`**: starts (or attaches to) two running Shiny apps, then compares what their served pages actually load: every stylesheet, every script, and any inline styles in the head, down to the bytes. It reports four kinds of difference: a file only one side loads, the same library under a different file name (for instance a stock CSS file on one side and a theme-compiled version on the other), and the same file name with different bytes. This is what found the Bootstrap 3 issue in #285: it showed `bootstrap-3.4.1` loading on the shinyreact side only.

**`peek.R`**: opens a running app in headless Chrome, waits for Shiny to connect and settle, then reports console errors, whether Shiny actually connected, how many inputs and outputs are bound, the html and body attributes, the stylesheets in load order, and the computed style and box of any element you point at with a CSS selector. Run it against two apps and it also prints where the two readouts differ. This is what showed the actual JavaScript exception stopping Shiny from finishing its connection, the thing that led to #285.

Both scripts work against any two URLs. Neither one assumes anything about a particular app; the "original" and "new app" framing in the code is just to make output readable when comparing a Shiny app to its conversion, but either argument can point at any Shiny app at all.

**What I'm asking**

Would something like this be useful under `examples/` or a new `tools/` folder, or as a documented recipe in one of the skill reference files? If yes, I'll clean these up properly (tests, a couple of rough edges I know about) and open a PR. If this overlaps with something already planned or already exists in a form I missed, pointing me at it would save me the work.

title: page_react() loads Bootstrap 3 by default, with no way to turn it off
description:
This is a preliminary finding. I found it while porting several Shiny apps to shinyreact's `ui.tsx` pattern, using the `shinyreact-convert-app` skill from this repo. Please check it and tell me if it holds up.

**Versions used:** `shiny` 1.14.0, `shinyreact` built from `main` at commit `3315946`.

**What I saw**

A `page_react()` app with no theme loads classic Bootstrap 3.4.1, plus its accessibility plugin, on every page. The app never asked for this and has no bslib theme at all.

This is not just extra weight. On one of my ports, Bootstrap 3's accessibility plugin threw a real error against a newer jQuery the app also loaded (for an unrelated widget), and that error stopped Shiny from finishing its connection. The page never became usable.

**Why it happens**

`page_bare()` calls `shiny::bootstrapPage(..., theme = ...)` directly. When `bootstrapPage()`'s own `theme` argument is `NULL`, which is what happens when nobody passes one, it attaches Bootstrap 3 unconditionally. This is Shiny's own long-standing default, not something shinyreact adds on purpose. `page_react()` and `page_bare()` just pass `theme` straight through, unchanged.

I don't think this is a shinyreact bug exactly. But it seems like a real gap for the `ui.tsx` pattern, since the docs already say the point of that pattern is that the client owns styling. A themeless app, by definition, wants to own every pixel, and it gets an unwanted Bootstrap 3 stack anyway, with no documented way to turn it off.

**A small repro**

```r
library(shiny)
library(shinyreact)
dir.create("www", showWarnings = FALSE)
writeLines("", "www/ui.js")

ui <- page_react(title = "no-theme")
server <- function(input, output, session) {}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Load the app and view the page source. `bootstrap-3.4.1/css/bootstrap.min.css` and `bootstrap-3.4.1/accessibility/js/bootstrap-accessibility.min.js` are both there.

**A fix I tested and it works**

Attaching `htmltools::suppressDependencies("bootstrap")` next to the page, not wrapping it, removes Bootstrap 3 entirely. jQuery and Shiny's own JS and CSS are untouched:

```r
ui <- page_react(title = "no-theme", htmltools::suppressDependencies("bootstrap"))
```

I also checked this is safe to use only when there is no real theme. `suppressDependencies()` works by attaching a dummy, empty dependency at a higher version number, and htmltools keeps only the highest version of a dependency with a given name. bslib's own compiled Bootstrap 5 uses the same dependency name, just a different version, so this same call would wrongly strip a real theme too if it ran unconditionally. I confirmed a `page_react(theme = bs_theme(version = 5))` app still loads its compiled Bootstrap 5 normally. So this fix stays correct only as long as it is applied in the themeless case, not always.

**What I'm asking**

Would it make sense for `page_bare()` or `page_react()` to offer an explicit way to skip Bootstrap 3 when there's no theme? Shiny's own `theme` argument has no way to say "no Bootstrap at all," only `NULL` for the classic default, a compiled theme, or a plain CSS link. Happy to open a PR with this if the shape (an argument name, where it lives) sounds right to you.

title: Build a shinyreact documentation website
description:
We should build a documentation website for `shinyreact`, mirroring the
setup used by [posit-dev/shinychat](https://posit-dev.github.io/shinychat/).

## Goals

- Landing page that explains what `shinyreact` is and links to the two
  first-class patterns (`app.py` and `ui.tsx`).
- Python API reference for `pkg-py/` (`page_react`, `ui_output`,
  `reactive_output`, `Spec` / `Element` / `Node`, `set_react_page`,
  `send_message`, …).
- R API reference for `pkg-r/` once the R package is implemented.
- JS API reference for the `window.shinyreact` global (`registerComponents`,
  `useShinyInput`, `useShinyInputValue`, `useSetShinyInput`,
  `useShinyOutputValue`, `useShinyOutputStatus`, `useShinyMessageHandler`,
  `useShinyInitialized`, `useShinyBusy`).
- Articles / vignettes covering:
  - `app.py` vs `ui.tsx` (already drafted in `docs/app-py-vs-ui-tsx.md`)
  - Downstream package authoring (the `shinyshadcn` pattern)
  - Examples gallery linking to `examples/app-py/` and `examples/ui-tsx/`
- Auto-deploy to GitHub Pages on push to `main` and on release tags.

## Reference setup (from shinychat)

shinychat's website is assembled from three pieces, all deployed to the
`gh-pages` branch:

1. **Landing page** — static HTML in `docs/` (`index.html`, `404.html`,
   `logo.svg`, `chat-styles.css`).
2. **Python API docs** — quartodoc + Quarto, sources in `pkg-py/docs/`,
   built by `.github/workflows/quartodoc.yaml` via `make py-docs-api &&
   quarto render pkg-py/docs`.
3. **R API docs** — pkgdown, sources in `pkg-r/pkgdown/`, built by
   `.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml`. R releases are gated on tags
   starting with `r/v*`.

All three publish into the same `gh-pages` branch with `clean: false` so
they coexist at different sub-paths under one site.

## What we don't have yet

- No `pkg-py/docs/`, no quartodoc config, no `make py-docs-api` target.
- No `pkg-r/pkgdown/` config (R package itself is still a placeholder per
  `CLAUDE.md`).
- No JS-side API doc generator wired up. The `window.shinyreact` surface
  is small — TypeDoc against `js/src/index.ts` is probably enough.
- No landing-page content / branding decisions.

## Related

The Great Docs roadmap describes a future [multi-language API
documentation](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-docs/roadmap.html#multi-language-api-documentation-python-r-rust-js)
system (one navbar / sidebar / search across Python, R, Rust, JS via
"language adapters", with cross-language "see also" links). That's the
ideal long-term target for a project like `shinyreact` that ships both
Python and JS (and eventually R) APIs side-by-side. For now we should
copy the shinychat approach (separate Quarto / pkgdown / TypeDoc builds
deployed to one Pages site) and migrate to the unified tooling when it
lands.

## Suggested checklist

- [ ] Scaffold `pkg-py/docs/` (Quarto + quartodoc `_quarto.yml`)
- [ ] Add `make py-docs-api` target + `quartodoc.yaml` workflow
- [ ] Scaffold `docs/` landing page (`index.html`, brand assets)
- [ ] Add TypeDoc (or equivalent) for `js/src/` public surface
- [ ] Wire JS docs into the Pages deploy
- [ ] Decide URL layout (e.g. `/` landing, `/py/`, `/r/`, `/js/`)
- [ ] Add `pkg-r/pkgdown/` config + `pkgdown.yaml` workflow once R
      package exists (gate on `r/v*` tags like shinychat does)
- [ ] Set repo `homepageUrl` to the Pages URL once published

title: Docs site: brand.yml styling for the Quarto / pkgdown / TypeDoc pages
description:
Follow-up to #86. The docs site (Quarto landing + quartodoc at `/py/`, pkgdown at `/r/`, TypeDoc at `/js/`) ships with stock themes: Quarto `cosmo`, pkgdown Bootstrap 5 default, TypeDoc default.

Give it one look across all three:

- [ ] Add `_brand.yml` (colors, fonts, `logo/shiny-react.svg`) and switch `pkg-py/docs/_quarto.yml` to `theme: [brand]` (shinychat does this)
- [ ] Point `pkg-r/_pkgdown.yml` at the same brand file (`template: brand:` is supported by pkgdown ≥ 2.1)

- [ ] Logo in the Quarto navbar / pkgdown home
- [ ] Set the repo `homepageUrl` to https://posit-dev.github.io/shinyreact/ once the first deploy lands

title: Relocate example apps into their respective packages
description:
Today `examples/` is a top-level tree with mixed-language apps (01-hello ships `app.py`, `app-core.py`, *and* `app.R` side by side), and the packages reach out of their own trees to use them — pytest `testpaths` covers `examples/`, `pkg-r/tests/testthat/test-examples.R` sources example testthat files and has to skip when `examples/` is absent (installed package), and the new `wire_tap()` e2e test needed a manual copy of 01-hello into `pkg-r/inst/examples-shiny/01-hello/` to be reachable from an installed package at all.

Proposal: move each example app into the package that runs it:

- **R apps** → `pkg-r/inst/examples-shiny/<name>/` — ships with the package, reachable via `system.file()` from any test tier (unit, `wire_tap()` e2e, future shinytest2 suite per #194), and available for `shiny::runExample()`-style discovery.
- **Python apps** → somewhere equivalently package-owned (e.g. `pkg-py/examples/` or shipped in the wheel), so the Playwright suite and `shiny run` docs don't depend on repo-root layout.
- **Shared assets** (`www/ui.js`, `FEATURES.md`, fixture data like `faithful.csv`) need a single source of truth with a copy step (the `make update-dist` pattern) or a parity test — the `inst/examples-shiny/01-hello/` copy added on the #201 branch is currently manual and will drift silently.

Benefits: installed-package tests stop skipping, no more out-of-tree path reach-through in test configs, each language's example is the idiomatic single-language app a user of that package expects, and the examples become usable API surface (`runExample()`) rather than repo furniture.

Coordinate with:
- #179 (prune the example set) — prune first so we relocate only the survivors.
- #217 (npm tier / convert 09-hmr) — affects which examples have a build step and where their bundles land.
- #194 (R Playwright/e2e suite) — the R suite wants package-reachable fixture apps, which this provides.

Origin: #201 research branch, where the `wire_tap()` R e2e test forced the first `inst/examples-shiny/` copy.
