title: npm tier: server-side switch to omit the IIFE bundle; convert examples/09-hmr to @posit/shinyreact
description:
Deferred from #215 (see `decisions/2026-08-17-js-distribution.md` status line).

## Problem

An app that bundles `@posit/shinyreact` (npm tier) ships its own copy of the hooks + React. But every page entry point (`page_react()`, `set_react_page()`, `page_react_html()`) unconditionally injects the IIFE `shinyreact.js` HTMLDependency too — so the page runs **two** runtimes, and both register the `shinyReactMessage` custom-message handler (double-dispatch) and their own registries.

## Needed

1. A server-side switch for npm-tier pages to omit the IIFE bundle while keeping the `#shinyreact-config` tag (protocol version + restore payload still required — the npm client hard-errors without the tag). Shape TBD, e.g. `page_react(runtime="external")` / `include_bundle=False` — pick one name and mirror it in R.
2. Convert `examples/09-hmr` to consume `@posit/shinyreact` (repo-relative `file:../../pkg-js` until the first npm publish): import hooks directly, delete the dev/prod `shiny-bridge` alias and the React-externalization vite config, bundle React (dev React + Fast Refresh in dev).
3. The example is the acceptance test: one runtime on the page, message handlers fire once, HMR works without the bridge workaround.

Refs #172, #215, `decisions/2026-08-17-js-distribution.md`.

title: Add an R Playwright e2e suite
description:
Split out of #185, which closed the R unit-test gaps. This is the one item left: R has no end-to-end tests.

## Why it is its own issue

The blocker is fixture infrastructure, not test cases. `pkg-py/tests/playwright/` stands up a Python Shiny app per fixture; an R suite needs an equivalent runner for R apps (`shiny::runApp()` in a subprocess, port allocation, readiness polling, teardown) before a single assertion can be written. That is a different kind of change from writing tests, so it did not belong in #185's PR.

## What to cover

The JS bundle is byte-identical between the two packages (`md5 335334fd88165d6906de2fd20c2ee174`), so an R suite is not re-testing the client — it validates the **R server bindings**. A subset of the Python suite is enough. Python currently covers:

- module namespaces
- module dependency injection
- bookmark restore
- input-handler types
- `ShinyOutput`

Bookmark restore and input-handler types are the highest value in R, since those are where the two servers' implementations actually differ (`pkg-r/R/bookmark.R` uses pinned `shiny:::` internals; `default_input_handler()` exists specifically to undo jsonlite/shiny simplification that Python never does).

Module dependency injection is likely **not** applicable — `set_react_page()`'s renderer-dependency harvesting is Shiny Express-only and has no R analogue by [an explicit decision](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinyreact/blob/main/decisions/2026-08-13-r-python-parity.md).

## Notes

- `decisions/2026-03-17-playwright-testing-architecture.md` records the recommended approach (code-gen from TypeScript) for browser testing generally; worth reading before picking a direction.
- The Makefile pattern to mirror: `py-test-e2e` clears the `addopts` that otherwise ignore the `playwright/` subtree, keeping `py-check-tests` fast.

title: Prune the example set
description: Follow-up from #168 (trim to ui.tsx pattern). The catalog now has 10 examples (01-hello … 10-bookmarking, with 01-hello shipping both app.py and app.R). Decide which survive long-term and remove the rest — candidates for consolidation include the two shadcn examples (03-columns-shadcn, 04-shadcn) and the two ShinyOutput embeds (06-data-frame, 07-plotly).

title: Expose the error message, not just `"error"` status, for erroring outputs
description:
## The gap

When a `reactive_output` errors, the client can only learn that it errored: `useShinyOutputStatus(id)` returns `"error"`, but the error *message* never reaches the app author's code. Vanilla Shiny shows the (sanitized) condition message in the output's error UI, so an app being converted to the ui.tsx pattern cannot reproduce its own original behavior.

This surfaced twice while porting the 10 stock `shiny::runExamples()` apps as a skills benchmark — both ports had to record it as a *forced* deliberate divergence rather than a choice:

- **08_html port**: the original renders R's error text (e.g. `invalid number of 'breaks'` from `hist()` at `n = 0`) in the output area; the port could only show a generic "Something went wrong." — "error text not reproduced verbatim since `reactive_output` only exposes status, not message."
- **09_upload port**: same story for `read.csv()` failures — "the error message is generic rather than threading the R condition text across the wire."

## Sketch

Thread the sanitized error message through the wire the way Shiny itself does (respecting `shiny.sanitize.errors` / `sanitize_errors`, and `req()`'s silent errors staying silent), and expose it client-side — either a new hook (e.g. `useShinyOutputError(id)` returning `{message} | null`) or by widening what the status channel carries. Applies to both languages; the registry already tracks per-output status, so the plumbing has a natural home.

## Acceptance sketch

- R and Python: an erroring `reactive_output` delivers its sanitized condition/exception message to the client.
- Client: the message is readable from a hook; `useShinyOutputStatus` semantics unchanged.
- Silent validation errors (`req()`, `validate()`) produce no message, matching Shiny.
- FEATURES.md leaves + tests in both languages per the parity policy.

title: Protocol handshake failure should be visible on the page, not only in DevTools
description:
## Problem

#198's protocol handshake fails fast and throws with a good message (both versions + remedy named), but the throw happens during the first hook mount — so the *page* just looks blank/broken. The message only exists in the DevTools console. A user (or a developer who hasn't opened DevTools) gets no explanation.

## Proposal

When `assertProtocolCompatible()` fails (and, once the npm tier exists, when the `#shinyreact-config` tag is missing entirely), surface the error visibly in the page in addition to throwing:

1. **Preferred: ride Shiny's existing client-side error surfaces.**
   - Shiny's client error console (the dev-mode error overlay) — if dev mode is on, the developer sees the mismatch the same place they see other Shiny client errors.
   - And/or `Shiny.notifications.show()` for a visible notification even outside dev mode.
   - Caveat to investigate: at handshake time (first hook mount) `window.Shiny` exists but the session may not be fully initialized; the chosen surface must work that early.
2. **Fallback: a plain DOM banner** appended to `document.body` before throwing — zero dependencies on Shiny being alive, works even when the bundle/server are too broken to talk to each other (which is exactly the failure being reported).

Whatever the surface, the visible text should match the thrown error: both protocol versions and which side to upgrade.

## Scenarios to cover

- Client major > server major (upgrade the R/Python package)
- Client major < server major (upgrade the client bundle / npm package)
- npm tier only, once it exists: `#shinyreact-config` tag absent (server predates the tag → treat as hard error in the npm build; the IIFE build keeps tolerating absence since it cannot skew and `page_bare()` pages legitimately lack the tag)

## Acceptance

- A protocol-mismatched page shows a human-readable explanation without opening DevTools; dev mode shows it in Shiny's error console.
- The error is still thrown (fail fast is unchanged); the notification is additive.
- Unit tests cover the notification path for both mismatch directions.

Refs #172, `decisions/2026-08-17-js-distribution.md` (handshake), PR #198.

title: set_react_page: automatically deliver dependencies for renderers registered after page load
description:
Follow-up to #87. Builds on the automatic dependency discovery shipped there (synchronously-mounted top-level + `@module.server` renderers) and the `@render.ui` dynamic-UI path (delivered natively by Shiny).

## Goal

Make the **server-registers-a-renderer-after-page-load + React-supplied placeholder** pattern work **automatically**, with no user ceremony. Example:

```python
@reactive.effect
@reactive.event(input.add)
async def _():
    @render_plotly
    def scatter():
        return px.scatter(...)
    get_current_session().output(scatter)   # registered after the page is built
```
…with the React client mounting `<ShinyOutput id="scatter" .../>`. Today the chart never renders: the renderer's `HTMLDependency` (the binding JS) was never delivered, so the element can't bind.

## What we already ruled in / out (investigation summary)

All verified with Playwright spikes against `shinywidgets` `render_plotly`:

1. **Value delivery is NOT the problem.** A dynamically-registered output sends its value fine; Shiny's `bindOutput` even replays a stored `$values[id]` when the element later binds. A dynamically-registered `render.text` (binding JS in core `shiny.js`) renders correctly.
2. **The problem is the missing dependency.** `dep_scripts=0 → bound=0 → no render`. Proof: a `ui.hold()`-ed warm-up `render_plotly` (so Layer A injects the binding JS at startup) makes the *dynamically* registered output render (`bound=1, plotly=1`).
3. **Naive late-push does NOT work for widgets.** Pushing the dep after registration + `renderDependenciesAsync` + `bindAll` fails with `Error: No model found for id …`. shinywidgets sends the widget model via a `comm_open` **custom message** alongside the value; because the dep (which registers the comm handler) loads *asynchronously after* `comm_open` arrives, the message is dropped and the model is never created. This is a fundamental **ordering** problem, not a timing tweak (retrying `bindAll` for 2.4s did not help — the model is gone).
4. **A re-trigger handshake DOES work** (`bound=1, plotly=1`): push deps → client loads them → client signals server → the output **recomputes** → shinywidgets re-sends `comm_open` with its handler now present.
5. **But auto-triggering that recompute is the open problem.** The handshake only worked when the renderer depended on a reactive that the deps-ready signal bumped (one line of user cooperation). Two no-cooperation triggers **failed**:
   - re-registering the renderer (`session.output(renderer)` again) → `bound=0`;
   - manually invalidating the output effect's context (`effect._ctx.invalidate()`) → `bound=0` (invalidation without Shiny's flush-scheduling pipeline doesn't drive the recompute).

## What "automatic" needs (remaining work)

A way to force a registered output to recompute through Shiny's **normal** reactive pipeline — without the user's renderer explicitly depending on a deps-ready signal. Candidate directions to explore:

- A supported force-invalidate-and-flush primitive (invalidate the output context **and** request a session flush), rather than the private `effect._ctx` poke that didn't drive the recompute.
- A `suspend_when_hidden`-based dance: register the dynamic output suspended/hidden, push deps, then reveal it so Shiny's resume-on-show recomputes it after deps load.
- A shinyreact-owned reactive that dynamic outputs implicitly depend on (would likely require wrapping the renderer at registration).

Interim opt-in fallback (proven, ~1 line): have the dynamic renderer depend on a shinyreact-provided "deps-ready" reactive so the existing reactive path recomputes it.

## Related
- #87 — automatic dep discovery for synchronously-mounted renderers (Layer A).
- Design/investigation notes: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-11-dynamic-renderer-dep-delivery-design.md`.

title: Audit findings: parity gaps, latent bugs, and test holes found auditing FEATURES.md
description:
`FEATURES.md` (the behavior tree) was audited leaf-by-leaf against all three packages, in both directions: is every claim true, and does the code do things no claim covers. The tree itself has been corrected. This issue tracks the **code-level** findings, which are real and unfixed.

Grouped by severity. Every item was verified against the source; the ones marked **verified live** were reproduced by running code.

## Probably-wrong code (not just undocumented)

1. **`[r]` the `#shinyreact-config` tag renders in `<body>`, not `<head>`, under `page_react()`** — *verified live*: `renderTags(page_react())` puts it in `$html`, not `$head`. `shinyreact_dep_page()` returns a bare `tagList` (`pkg-r/R/dep.R:28-30`), whereas Python wraps it in `head_content()` (`_bookmark.py:84`). R's *other* path (`page_react_html()` → `config_head_dep()`) is head-correct, so R is inconsistent with itself as well as with Python. It works — the client finds the tag by id either way — but it is an unrecorded divergence.

2. **`[r]` `page_react_html()` does not preserve the document body verbatim** — *verified live*: `htmlTemplate()` evaluates **every** `{{ ... }}` in the document as R code with `parent = globalenv()`, so a body containing `{{ 6*7 }}` renders `42`. Any Vite/Handlebars document with `{{ }}` in the body is rewritten or errors. Python's marker handling is a plain replace and has no such behavior.

3. **`[js]` a forged `window.shinyreact._restore` silently disables restore *and* the protocol handshake** — `bookmark.ts:36-40` returns early on a truthy `"-applied"`, before `assertProtocolCompatible()` runs, with no warning. Intended as idempotence; the side effect is a kill switch.

4. **`[js]` `@posit/shinyreact` (npm build) ships no CSS** — `npm.ts` has no stylesheet import and `package.json` exposes no `./styles` export or `style` field, so consumers get no `@keyframes spin` and `ImageOutput`'s placeholder spinner does not animate. The IIFE bundle imports the CSS as a side effect; the ESM build does not.

5. **`[js]` output cleanup can remove the wrong DOM node** — `output-registry.ts:207` looks the div up with a document-global `getElementById(outputId)`, so an id collision with user markup removes the user's node.

6. **`[js]` `initializeMessageRegistry()` is a silent no-op without `window.Shiny`, with no retry** — so if Shiny loads after the first hook call, message handlers never register. The input registry deliberately tolerates a missing Shiny; this asymmetry looks unintended. `message-registry.ts` has **zero tests**.

7. **`[r]` `utils` is used but declared nowhere** — `getFromNamespace()` (`bookmark.R:40,49,57`) and `packageVersion()` (`dep.R:11`) with no `DESCRIPTION` or `NAMESPACE` entry.

## Parity gaps

8. **input-handler argument order differs**: `[py]` `(value, name, session)` (Shiny's `InputHandlerType`), `[r]` `(value, session, name)`. Both ignore the last two, so nothing catches it — but the signatures are documented as if shared.

9. **`page_react_html()` file encoding**: `[r]` decodes UTF-8 explicitly (via `htmlTemplate()`); `[py]` uses `Path.read_text()` with **no `encoding=`**, i.e. the platform locale (`_page.py:356,450`).

10. **`[r]` restore precision is globally overridable**: `shiny:::toJSON`'s `digits` is `getOption("shiny.json.digits", I(16))` — *verified live*: `options(shiny.json.digits = 2)` truncates `3.14159265358979` to `3.14` in the restore payload. Python has no equivalent global.

11. **`[py]` private-API use has no containment policy**: reads `session.output._outputs` (`_page.py:407`) and imports `shiny.bookmark._restore_state` (`_bookmark.py:6-9`) inline. R confines its internals to named `shiny___*` wrappers with a `shiny (>= 1.13.0)` pin — though not totally: `ctx$input$asList()` (`bookmark.R:81`) calls a private R6 method directly.

## Robustness / rough edges

12. **`[r]` a missing `src_dir` degrades to `"."`** — *verified live*: no `www/` yields `<title>.</title>` and a dependency named `.`, served at `/lib/.-0/`. No error, no test.
13. **`[r]` the marker check is `fixed = TRUE`**, so `{{headContent()}}` is rejected even though `htmlTemplate()` would accept it.
14. **the marker check is not `<head>`-scoped** in either language: a `{{ headContent() }}` in `<body>` passes and deps render there, though the error message asserts `<head>`.
15. **`[py]` `ReactApp` latches its mode at construction** (`_app.py:81`), so creating/deleting `www/index.html` after startup never switches modes — even though the UI is per-request. Relatedly, the per-request UI re-runs `page_react`'s existence checks and re-emits the missing-`ui.js` warning on **every request**.
16. **`[py]` `static_assets` edges, both untested**: explicit `static_assets=None` still auto-mounts (the guard is `is None`), and a passed value *replaces* rather than merges, leaving the document's directory unserved.
17. **`[js]` `useShinyOutputValue` does not reset its held value when the id/namespace changes**, so the old id's data stays visible.
18. **`[js]` `MISSING` does not cancel a pending debounced send**, so a real value written just before it still lands on the server.
19. **`[js]` conflicting `priority` across mounts is silently last-writer-wins**, while conflicting `type` throws.
20. **`[js]` `initializeReactRegistry()` is not idempotent** (a second call discards all values); `getReactRegistry()` returns `undefined` unchecked when Shiny is present but init never ran, and throws otherwise; the output container is created with **no `document` guard**, so init throws in a DOM-less environment — the opposite of the lifecycle store's stated policy.
21. **`[js]` every manufactured output div ships the literal text** `This is the output div for <id>` into the page.
22. **`[js]` `ShinyReactComponentElement.disconnectedCallback` calls `unbindAll(this)` without `includeSelf`**, so the element itself is never unbound — the inverse of `ShinyOutput`'s carefully reasoned choice.
23. **`[js]` the protocol handshake is skipped when `protocolVersion` is absent or falsy** (`config.ts:16-20`, `bookmark.ts:50`), so a tagged page carrying no version silently skips version checking.

## Test holes worth closing

24. **`shiny-bound-output` is asserted nowhere** — it appears only as a comment in `pkg-py/tests/playwright/test_shiny_output.py:24`. One-line fix: `expect(out).to_have_class(re.compile(r"\bshiny-bound-output\b"))`.
25. **`[r]` the bundle script's `defer` attribute is unpinned** — Python pins its script attrs; R pins only `src`. This is precisely the #182 failure mode.
26. **the bundle-version fallback divergence is tested in neither language** — `[py]` `"0.1.0"` vs `[r]` `packageVersion("shinyreact")`.
27. **`.tagify()` in the renderer harvest is unpinned** — `test_react_page_harvests_session_output_deps` still passes with the call deleted.
28. **`page_react()`'s "no body HTML" is asserted in neither language** — and it is false in R (finding 1).
29. **`__all__` / `NAMESPACE` export sets are pinned by no test** in either language.
30. **`[js]` the 15-item `window.shinyreact` surface has no test** — the object literal and the `Window` interface would drift together silently.
31. Also unpinned: `page_bare()` emitting no config tag, `set_react_page`'s explicit-missing-path error, renderer harvest in *discovered* mode, `[r]` `send_message`'s `invisible(NULL)`, `[r]` `force = TRUE` in `.onLoad()`, `[js]` `debounceMs`'s numeric default, and every `ImageOutput` leaf except namespace precedence.

## Not actionable, recorded for honesty

Twelve leaves are **UNVERIFIABLE** as written — rationale and policy claims with no code to check: the protocol's "bumps only when a boundary shape changes" (no test fails when it does not), `<script defer>` throwing on a module import, htmltools dep de-duplication, `MISSING` → `SilentException` (cross-language, unpinned), and "re-binding the parent is safe because Shiny skips bound elements" (mocked in unit tests). They are marked in the tree rather than dropped.

title: Packaging strategy for downstream renderer packages (Python + JS)
description:
## Summary

Downstream renderer packages (e.g. `shinyplotly`, `shinyshadcn`, `shinymui`) need both a Python side (`@render_plotly`, Spec/Element builders, `HTMLDependency`) and a JS side (React components registered via `window.shinyreact.registerComponents`). This issue settles **how those packages should be structured, built, distributed, and consumed**.

Establishes the shape; the per-framework rollout in #32 then follows it.

## Design decisions

### 1. Audience: serve both populations equally

A `shinyplotly`-style package must work for:

- **Pure-Python users** — `pip install shinyplotly`, write `@render_plotly` in `app.py`, never touch `npm`. The JS comes along for the ride via `HTMLDependency`.
- **SPA/Vite users** — `npm install @shinyreact/plotly`, `import { Plotly } from \"@shinyreact/plotly\"` in their JSX, *and* still use `@render_plotly` server-side.

Neither audience should have to do the other's setup.

### 2. Repo layout: one source, two publish targets

Single repository per package family with the same shape this repo already uses:

```
shinyplotly/
├── js/                          # TS/React source
│   ├── src/
│   ├── dist/                    # Built artifacts (committed)
│   ├── package.json             # npm publish source
│   └── vite.config.{iife,esm}.ts
├── pkg-py/
│   └── src/shinyplotly/
│       ├── __init__.py          # render_plotly, dep(), Spec helpers
│       └── www/                 # IIFE bundle copied from js/dist (committed)
├── pkg-r/                       # optional, future
└── pyproject.toml
```

CI builds **two artifacts** from `js/src/`:

- An **IIFE bundle** copied to `pkg-py/src/shinyplotly/www/` and bundled into the Python wheel. Loaded in pure-Python apps via the package's `HTMLDependency`.
- An **ESM package** with TypeScript types, published to npm as `@shinyreact/<name>`. Imported directly by SPA/Vite users.

Single source of truth, single version number, two distribution channels. Mirrors what `shinyreact` itself already does (`js/` + `pkg-py/`), just adds an `npm publish` step.

### 3. Dependency registration: `ui_output(id, extra_deps=[...])` — not on `reactive_output`

The Python `HTMLDependency` from a downstream package is **passed via `ui_output`**, not via the renderer. `reactive_output` (the unified decorator) no longer carries `extra_deps`:

```python
from shiny import App
from shinyreact import SpaApp
from shinyplotly import render_plotly, dep as plotly_dep

def server(inputs, output, session):
    @render_plotly
    def my_plot():
        return px.scatter(df, x=\"x\", y=\"y\")

app = SpaApp(server, extra_deps=[plotly_dep()])
```

Rejected alternatives:

- **Auto-sniff via mock session.** Run `server()` once with a fake session at `SpaApp` init to observe which renderers were declared, harvest their `extra_deps`. Rejected: real `server()` functions have side effects (DB pools, observers, async tasks); running them twice is fragile and surprising.
- **Import-time side-effect registration.** `import shinyplotly` registers its dep into a `shinyreact._registry`; `SpaApp` reads the registry. Rejected as too magic — globals that change behavior based on import order are a debugging trap.
- **Renderer-list constructor arg.** `SpaApp(server, renderers=[render_plotly])`. Rejected: just shifts the verbosity without the explicitness payoff that `extra_deps=[...]` gives.

Manual is more verbose but **predictable**. We can revisit if the friction proves real.

### 4. Double-load handling: JS-side idempotence

When an SPA/Vite user installs **both** the npm package and the Python package, the same JS would otherwise load twice — once from the user's Vite bundle, once from the `HTMLDependency`-served IIFE. That causes duplicate React component registrations and possibly duplicate copies of heavyweight deps (e.g. `plotly.js`).

Solution: every published bundle (both IIFE and ESM) uses a tiny shared idempotence pattern:

```ts
// pseudocode shared across all downstream packages
const REGISTRY = (window.shinyreact.registered ??= new Set());
if (REGISTRY.has(\"@shinyreact/plotly\")) {
  // already loaded — short-circuit
} else {
  REGISTRY.add(\"@shinyreact/plotly\");
  window.shinyreact.registerComponents(catalog, registry);
  // …rest of one-time setup
}
```

User can pass `extra_deps=[plotly_dep()]` redundantly with no harm. The runtime is the single source of truth.

Rejected alternatives:

- **\"User's responsibility\" / docs only.** Footgun — failure mode is silent (duplicate registrations) or obscure (two plotly copies fighting over a `<canvas>`). Not acceptable.
- **`SpaApp(suppress_deps=[\"@shinyreact/plotly\"])` flag.** Just (A) with extra ceremony.

This pattern should live in a tiny shared helper (probably exported from `@shinyreact/core` or `window.shinyreact` itself) so each downstream package writes one line, not the boilerplate above.

## What this enables

- A `shinyplotly` package can be authored once and consumed both ways.
- The npm-bindings rollout (#32) has a concrete template to follow.
- Renderer enhancement (#31) — round-trip inputs and command methods on the renderer class — composes cleanly: the round-trip input contract is part of the package's TS types, and #30's typegen sees it.
- Adding a new framework binding becomes a recipe (\"copy this repo template, replace the components, bump the npm/PyPI names\") rather than a design exercise.

## Open questions

- **Where does the shared idempotence helper live?** Three options: `@shinyreact/core` (clean, but creates an npm dependency for the IIFE case where externalizing isn't natural), inline in each package (~20 LOC duplication), or attached to `window.shinyreact` at runtime (no build-time dependency, but ad-hoc API surface). Lean toward `window.shinyreact.registerOnce(name, fn)` — already at runtime, no extra packages.
- **Versioning across npm + PyPI.** Same version number for both? Or independent semver? Recommend same version, single git tag drives both publishes.
- **`pkg-r/` for downstream packages.** Out of scope for v1, but the layout reserves space.
- **Build tooling**: Vite (matches what we already use) vs. tsup vs. unbuild. Probably Vite for parity with the rest of the repo.
- **Template repo**: do we ship `posit-dev/shinyreact-binding-template` so external authors can clone and go? Likely yes once the first 1–2 in-house packages prove the shape.
- **Component naming collisions across packages.** `@shinyreact/shadcn` and `@shinyreact/mui` both want a `Button`. The `registerComponents` registry is global. Either namespace at registration (`shadcn:Button`, `mui:Button`) or last-write-wins with a console warning. Lean toward namespacing.
- **Treeshaking the ESM build.** SPA users importing one component shouldn't pull the whole package. Standard ESM hygiene; call it out in the template.

## Relationship to other issues

- **Depends on #28** — \"Shiny client runtime as an npm package.\" Without it, downstream npm packages have to peer-depend on a non-published `@shinyreact/core` or vendor the IIFE.
- **Pairs with #30** — typed Inputs/Outputs codegen reads the TS types each downstream package ships.
- **Pairs with #31** — enhanced renderers (round-trip inputs + command methods) are how Python sees the components a downstream package contributes.
- **Implements the substrate for #32** — concrete bindings (`shadcn`, `mui`, `bootstrap`, …) follow this template.

## Out of scope

- R package equivalents.
- Frameworks other than React (Vue/Svelte/Solid).
- A monorepo umbrella (`@shinyreact/bindings`) shipping all official bindings under one tree — start with one repo per package, revisit if maintenance pressure makes a monorepo attractive.

title: Umbrella: unified UI component class for Shiny Core and Express
description:
# Umbrella: unified UI component class for Shiny Core and Express

## Summary

Replace the current "function returns `Tag`" UI surface with a class-per-component model. Each UI component becomes a `Tagifiable` Python class that owns its own metadata (children, HTML dependencies, input handler, bookmark serializer, `update()` method). Existing `ui.card(...)`, `ui.input_slider(...)` call sites stay the same — they become thin factory functions returning instances. The class is also exposed (e.g. `ui.UiCard`, `ui.UiInputSlider`) for type hints and `isinstance` checks.

This umbrella tracks three independently-shippable child issues, all prototyped in `shinyreact` first and then proposed upstream once the team accepts the design.

> Full design: [`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-06-unified-ui-component-class-design.md`](../docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-06-unified-ui-component-class-design.md)

## Why now

Three pain points the current design cannot fix without architectural change:

- **Per-component metadata is fragmented.** A date input's input handler, bookmark serializer, UI factory, and update function each live in a different file. Adding a new input requires touching four places; the relationships are implicit.
- **Core and Express need different code paths today.** Express uses `RecallContextManager` to convert function calls inside a `with` block into children. Core needs children passed positionally. Two functions, two mental models.
- **`Tag` is not a context manager.** The Express ergonomic win — `with ui.div(): ui.h1("x")` reading top-to-bottom — only works inside Express. The same idiom outside Express (or in a hybrid app) does not work.

`shinyreact` is the right venue for the prototype: small surface area, no entrenched user base, breaking changes are cheap. `py-shiny` is the wrong place to discover that an API doesn't feel right.

## Class hierarchy

Three sibling categories under `UiComponent`, plus an opt-in `AllowsChildren` mixin:

```
UiComponent                 # base: tagify(), html_dependencies, default __enter__ that raises
  ├── UiInput               # adds: id, input_handler_name, bookmark_serializer (class default + per-instance override), update()
  ├── UiOutput              # adds: id (no input handler, no bookmark serializer; consumes @render.* values)
  └── UiLayout              # container category; no id (most have AllowsChildren). Pages live here too.
```

| Concrete class                                   | Bases                          |
|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| `UiInputSlider`, `UiInputSelect`, ...            | `UiInput`                      |
| `UiOutputCode`, `UiOutputText`, ...              | `UiOutput`                     |
| `UiCard`, `UiSidebar`, `UiPageFluid`, ...        | `UiLayout, AllowsChildren`     |
| `UiNavsetTab`, `UiAccordion` (straddle)          | `UiInput, AllowsChildren`      |

The rule: **you can `with X(...)` if and only if `X` declares `AllowsChildren` in its bases.** A childless layout is expressible; a future input wanting children is too.

## Public API shape

Each component exposes two public symbols:

```python
class UiCard(UiLayout, AllowsChildren):
    def __init__(self, *args, full_screen: bool = False, ...): ...
    def tagify(self) -> Tag: ...

def card(*args, full_screen: bool = False, ...) -> UiCard:
    return UiCard(*args, full_screen=full_screen, ...)
```

`ui.card(...)` stays the user-facing API (overloads, validation, deprecation shims live here). `ui.UiCard` is the public class for type hints and `isinstance`.

## Out of the hierarchy

- **Server-triggered functions** (`modal_show`, `notification_show`, `insert_ui`, `Progress`) — imperative, not renderable.
- **Pure HTML helpers** (`tags.*`, `HTML`, `markdown`, `tooltip`, `popover`, `help_text`) — no Shiny lifecycle.
- **Configuration objects** (`Theme`, `SidebarOptions`, brand.yml, fill helpers) — passed to components, not components themselves.

## Two-stage delivery

- **Stage A — prototype in `shinyreact`.** Build the hierarchy and a small reference set (~6 classes covering all archetypes). Validate ergonomics, lifecycle, multi-inheritance, and Tag-as-CM against working example apps.
- **Stage B — upstream adoption.** After team acceptance, port the hierarchy into `py-shiny` (issues 1 & 2) and `py-htmltools` (issue 3).

## Child issues

- [ ] **#69 — Metadata consolidation.** `UiComponent` / `UiInput` / `UiOutput` / `UiLayout` / `AllowsChildren`, plus reference component classes. (Stage A: shinyreact. Stage B: py-shiny.)
- [ ] **#71 — Core/Express unification.** Single overloaded signature per class that works inline and as a context manager. Depends on #69. (Stage A: shinyreact. Stage B: py-shiny.)
- [ ] **#70 — Tag as context manager.** `__enter__` / `__exit__` plus a parent-tag context stack on `Tag`. Independent. (Stage A: prototyped via Tag subclass/wrapper in shinyreact. Stage B: py-htmltools.)

## Acceptance gate (Stage A → Stage B)

Before any upstream work begins, the team reviews the `shinyreact` prototype:

- Working example app demonstrating all archetypes.
- Bookmark round-trip, `update()` from server, Express + Core in one project.
- Snapshot tests confirming `tagify()` output matches equivalent `py-shiny` rendering.
- Documented open questions resolved or explicitly deferred.

If the design needs revision, it's revised in `shinyreact` first.

## Open questions (resolved at child-issue scoping)

- Handler registration mechanism: explicit module-load call vs. decorator. Both are explicit; pick one.
- Bookmark id → class instance lookup at session-attach time.
- `update()` signature: `**kwargs` mirroring today vs. typed per-class fields.
- Coexistence of Express's `RecallContextManager` and the new Tag stack.

## Risks

- **Prototype/upstream drift.** Mitigation: snapshot tests reused upstream; deliberate file-by-file porting pass.
- **Prototype acceptance never happens.** Mitigation: bring the team in early, while the prototype is small.
- **Hidden coupling on `isinstance(x, Tag)`** at Stage B. Mitigation: pre-flight grep across py-shiny and downstream packages.
- **Diamond/MRO** in straddling classes. Mitigation: `AllowsChildren` is a strict mixin (no `__init__` cooperation).
- **Issue 3 affects every htmltools consumer.** Mitigation: feature is opt-in semantically; safe-by-default outside `with`.

title: Tag as context manager + parent-tag context stack
description:
# Tag as context manager + parent-tag context stack

Part of umbrella #68 — unified UI component class for Shiny Core and Express.
**Independent** — does not depend on issues 1 or 2; can land in either order.

## Goal

Make any htmltools `Tag` usable as a context manager. Inside `with some_tag: ...`, any `Tag` constructed appends itself to `some_tag.children` automatically. No Shiny dependency — this is a generic htmltools feature.

## Why

The Express ergonomic win — `with ui.div(): ui.h1("x")` reading top-to-bottom — is currently implemented via `RecallContextManager`, which only works inside Shiny Express. Tag-as-CM brings the same idiom to:

- Pure htmltools usage (Quarto, standalone scripts).
- Shiny Core apps that want Express-style nesting in one section.
- Downstream packages that build on htmltools without depending on Shiny.

It also removes a subtle constraint from the unified-class design (umbrella issues 1 & 2): components no longer need their own bespoke context-manager logic — they get it for free from the underlying `Tag`.

## Approach

Two pieces, both in py-htmltools:

1. **Parent-tag context stack** — module-level `contextvars.ContextVar` holding a stack of currently-entered `Tag`s. Safe under async and multiple concurrent contexts.
2. **`Tag.__enter__` / `__exit__`** — entering pushes self onto the stack and returns self. Exiting pops. While a `Tag` is on top of the stack, any newly-constructed `Tag` (or any `Tagifiable` registered via the same hook) appends itself to the top tag's `children`.

## Stage A — prototype in `shinyreact`

Two viable approaches; Stage A picks one and validates the mechanics:

- A `Tag` subclass (e.g. `CtxTag`) exported from `shinyreact` that adds the context-manager behavior. Used by the issue 1 reference classes' `tagify()` outputs.
- A wrapper class around `Tag` providing the same surface.

### Stage A acceptance

- [ ] `with shinyreact_tag(...) as d: child_a(); child_b()` produces the expected DOM in a `shinyreact` example.
- [ ] Stack is contextvars-based; safe under concurrent sessions (test with two simultaneous Shiny sessions in one process).
- [ ] `Tagifiable` instances appended into a parent's children continue to render correctly via the parent's `tagify()`.
- [ ] Children appear in source order in the rendered output.

## Stage B — upstream adoption in `py-htmltools`

After Stage A acceptance, propose the change to py-htmltools maintainers:

- [ ] Add `__enter__` / `__exit__` to `Tag` itself (no Shiny subclass needed).
- [ ] Implement the parent-tag context stack at the module level.
- [ ] Document as a top-level htmltools feature.
- [ ] Confirm no breakage for existing consumers (Quarto, standalone uses) — the feature is opt-in semantically (you only see the behavior if you write `with tag:`).

### Stage B acceptance

- [ ] `with div(class_="x") as d: h1("title"); p("body")` produces the expected DOM in pure htmltools (no Shiny).
- [ ] Existing htmltools test suite passes unchanged.
- [ ] Quarto's Python integration verified unbroken on a sample doc.

## Coordination with Shiny Express (post-Stage B)

A follow-up `py-shiny` PR can migrate Express's child-collection to use the new Tag stack where it cleans up code. Until then, the two coexist:

- `RecallContextManager` continues to capture *function calls* at the script-body level.
- The Tag stack captures *Tag construction* inside `with` blocks.

Where both could apply, the inner-most active mechanism wins (likely the Tag stack, since `with` blocks are explicitly scoped). This needs a tiebreaker rule documented in the migration follow-up, not in this issue.

## Out of scope

- Refactoring Express's `RecallContextManager` to use the new stack — separate follow-up.
- Generalizing context-manager support to non-`Tag` types beyond `Tagifiable`.
- Performance optimization of the stack mechanism beyond "no measurable regression on existing benchmarks."

## Risks

- **Quarto and other htmltools consumers.** Mitigation: opt-in semantically (no behavior change unless user writes `with tag:`); demonstrate concretely in `shinyreact` Stage A before pitching upstream.
- **Async safety.** Mitigation: `contextvars.ContextVar` (not threading-locals); test with concurrent Shiny sessions.
- **Confusion with Express's existing `with` machinery.** Mitigation: clear coexistence rules documented in the follow-up migration.

title: Core/Express unification: one signature per component, two modes
description:
# Core/Express unification: one signature per component, two modes

Part of umbrella #68 — unified UI component class for Shiny Core and Express.
**Depends on** issue #69 (metadata consolidation).

## Goal

Each component class exposes a single overloaded signature that type-checks correctly when used inline (Core: `card(child_a, child_b, full_screen=True)`) and as a context manager (Express: `with card(full_screen=True): ...`). One symbol, two modes, no separate `core.card` vs. `express.card` namespaces.

## Approach

Use `@overload` to declare two signatures on `__init__`:

- **First overload — Express mode (no positional children).** IDEs prefer this when the user types `with card(...)`. Docstring describes context-manager usage.
- **Second overload — Core mode (positional children).** IDEs match this when the user passes children. Docstring describes inline usage.
- **Implementation** is a single `__init__` accepting both shapes; runtime branches based on whether positional args were supplied.

Mode mixing (e.g. `with card(child, ...):`) raises with a clear message at `__enter__` time, not silently.

## Stage A — prototype in `shinyreact`

- [ ] Add overloaded `__init__` signatures to the reference component classes from issue 1 (at minimum: `UiCard`, one straddling class).
- [ ] Express overload appears first so IDEs prefer it.
- [ ] Mixing modes raises `TypeError` with a message naming the component and the conflict.
- [ ] Example app demonstrates the same component used in both modes within the same project.

### Stage A acceptance

- [ ] `card(*args, ...)` and `with card(...):` both type-check on the reference classes.
- [ ] Hovering on `card` in an IDE inside a `with` block shows the Express docstring; hovering on inline use shows the Core docstring.
- [ ] Mixing modes raises with a clear message.
- [ ] Pyright clean on a small example file exercising both modes.

## Stage B — upstream adoption in `py-shiny`

- [ ] Apply the validated overload pattern to every component class from issue 1's Stage B.
- [ ] Confirm IDE behavior in Pyright and Pylance against representative apps.
- [ ] Update Express documentation to point at the unified API rather than the `RecallContextManager` mechanism.

### Stage B acceptance

- [ ] Every component class has the dual overload.
- [ ] Express usage continues to render the same children in the same order as today.
- [ ] No new error cases at runtime for users who don't change their code.

## Out of scope

- Generalizing the context-manager mechanism to all `Tag`s — that's umbrella issue 3.
- Replacing Express's `RecallContextManager`. Coexistence is fine for now; the eventual migration is a follow-up after issue 3 lands.

## Open questions to resolve in this issue

- **Order of overloads.** Express first (so `with` users get the right hover) or Core first (so inline users get the right hover)? Current lean: Express first, since the inline call is the historical default and pyright will fall through correctly.
- **Mode-mixing error wording.** Should it tell the user how to fix it, link to docs, or just name the conflict? Current lean: name the conflict + one-line "use one of these two patterns" example.

title: Browser-verify ui-frameworks galleries: static checks miss runtime crashes
description:
## Problem

Several `ui-frameworks` example/gallery apps shipped that **built, imported, type-checked, and passed `R CMD check` / ruff cleanly — but crashed or rendered blank at runtime in the browser.** Static checks do not exercise the rendered React tree or the Shiny session, so this whole class of bug slips through. Each was only caught by actually driving the app in a browser.

Bugs found this way (all in `ui-frameworks/`):

1. **Typography blanked the whole tree** (MUI error #7, `capitalize` expects a string). An optional Python arg defaulted to `None` → JSON `null` → the bridge passed `align={null}`; MUI calls `capitalize(null)` and throws, unmounting everything. Build/import were clean.
2. **`'Node' object is not iterable`** server-side serialization crash. The `mui.list` helper is named `list`, shadowing Python's builtin inside `_display.py`, so `children=list(children)` called the *list component* and produced `children=<Node>`. Import succeeded; only rendering threw.
3. **Dropped `async def toast`** → `AttributeError: module has no attribute 'toast'` → the async reactive crashed the Shiny session (looks like a hang/timeout). Root cause: a refactor splitter matched `ast.FunctionDef` but not `ast.AsyncFunctionDef`, and the parity check used `grep '^def '`, which also misses `async def` — so parity falsely passed.
4. **Stale bundle served.** `_dep()` preferred a gitignored build-time `www/` copy over the fresh shared one, so a stale bundle shadowed rebuilds during development.
5. **`gallery-r` silently drifted** out of parity with `gallery-py` (4 tabs/23 components vs 7 tabs/43) and was never caught.

## Why static checks miss it

`npm run build`, `tsc`, `vitest`, `uv build`, `import`, `R CMD check`, and `ruff` all verify that code **compiles, imports, and serializes** — not that components **mount and run** in a browser against a live Shiny session. Runtime React errors (a thrown `capitalize`, a portal failure) and server-side render/reactive exceptions only appear when the app is actually driven.

There is also **no CI coverage for `ui-frameworks/`** at all (the `check-*` workflows are path-filtered to `js/**`, `pkg-py/**`, `pkg-r/**`), so nothing automated runs these apps.

## Proposal

1. **A Claude skill** (`verify-ui-components`) that browser-drives a shinyreact example/gallery app (Python *and* R), clicks through every tab/category, and captures **both** the client console/page errors **and** the server-side traceback — plus a symptom→cause→fix playbook for the bug classes above. (Tracked here; first version added alongside this issue.)
2. **Follow-up: CI e2e for `ui-frameworks/` galleries** — a Playwright job that loads each gallery, exercises tabs, and asserts zero console/page errors and no server traceback, so this class of regression is caught automatically.

## Acceptance

- A documented, repeatable way to render-verify a shinyreact UI app (serve + headless browser + dual-sided error capture).
- The five bug classes above are encoded as a diagnosis table.
- (Stretch) a CI job runs it for the shadcn + MUI galleries.

title: R tag boolean/NA attribute serialization differs from Python

title: Claude Skill for scaffolding shinyjson apps
description:
## Summary

Build a Claude Skill (or equivalent agent tooling) that reliably scaffolds shinyreact apps in the SPA-first model. The SPA-first architecture is explicit that AI is the default path for generating the React client (`DESIGN.md:259-272, 290, 345`), so a managed, opinionated skill is core infrastructure — not optional polish.

The author writes `app.py` (reactive logic). The skill produces the rest: `index.html`, `package.json`, `vite.config.{ts,js}`, `src/main.{tsx,jsx}`, `src/App.{tsx,jsx}`, plus any feature-specific components. The skill is the bridge between \"developer thinks in reactive Python\" and \"correct React client wired through `useShinyInput`/`useShinyOutput`/`useShinyMessageHandler`\".

> **Updated:** Templates must offer **both** patterns (traditional JSON-spec and SPA) and use the unified API names: `reactive_output` and `send_message`.

## Why now

- The SPA-first split shipped (#26). The client is now hand-rolled per app and the boilerplate (Vite config, externalize React, IIFE vs ESM, `window.shinyreact` wiring) is the same every time — exactly the kind of thing a skill should encode.
- Examples 13–16 are starting to drift in style (build-free in 13/14, Vite/shadcn in 15/16). Without a skill, every new example is a fresh judgment call.
- The companion issues (#30, #31, #32, #33) all assume a generation/scaffolding step exists; a real skill is the place those design decisions become enforceable defaults.
- Roadmap already calls this out: `docs/timeline.md:70`, `docs/timeline.md:124`, and four spots in `DESIGN.md` (261, 290, 333, 345).

## Scope

### What the skill should generate

- **Greenfield app** — given a description (\"two columns, drag items between them\") + an `app.py` (or generated from the description), produce the full client side.
- **Migration** — take an existing traditional Shiny app and convert it (UI extracted from R/Python, reactive logic preserved, client regenerated). Called out in `DESIGN.md:288-290` as a strategic on-ramp.
- **Component additions** — \"add a chart that responds to row selection\" against an existing scaffolded app, without rewriting unrelated files.
- **Re-generation** — when `app.py` changes (new outputs, new inputs), regenerate just the affected client files without trampling user edits to JSX.

### What the skill should know

- The full `useShinyInput` / `useShinyOutput` / `useShinyMessageHandler` / `useShinyInitialized` hook contract — including subtleties already captured in `CLAUDE.md` (action button pattern, `defaultValue` stabilization, `priority: \"event\"`).
- The `SpaApp` + `reactive_output` API and how the Python and JS sides share names.
- The standard Vite lib-mode IIFE config with React externalized to `window.shinyreact` (today's ex-15/16 pattern) — and when *not* to use it (build-free apps like ex-13/14).
- `extra_deps` wiring for downstream packages (when introducing a `shinyplotly`/`shinyshadcn` dependency, where to add the dep, how to import the components in JSX). Ties to #33.
- The renderer round-trip pattern (#31) — how a custom renderer's round-trip inputs surface in JSX and back in Python.
- The component-naming and registration conventions (#33's idempotence pattern, #32's framework bindings).

### Constrained generation surface

`DESIGN.md:269` is the constraint for this skill: reliability comes as much from limiting the generation space as from improving the model. The skill should pick from a small menu of known-good shapes:

- File layout: fixed (`src/main.tsx`, `src/App.tsx`, `vite.config.ts`, `index.html`, `package.json`).
- Build target: IIFE for `SpaApp`-served pages; ESM only when the user explicitly opts into a multi-page or external-host setup.
- React version + externals: pinned, single source of truth.
- State patterns: enumerated (\"single source of truth in Python\", \"client-derived state from a single round-trip input\", \"event input via action-button pattern\"). The skill names the pattern in a comment so reviewers see what was chosen.

### Validation pipeline

`DESIGN.md:263-272` insists generation isn't trustworthy without validation. The skill should produce, alongside the code, the checks that prove it works:

- **Type check** — `tsc --noEmit` on generated TS.
- **Lint** — repo-standard `eslint`/`tsc` config.
- **Smoke test** — start the app, hit `/`, verify HTTP 200 + that the bundle paths resolve (the failure mode we hit live in this session for ex-15/16).
- **Browser e2e (later)** — Playwright assertions on the input→output round trip, per `DESIGN.md:271`.

Validation runs as part of the skill, not as user homework.

## Non-goals

- Replacing thoughtful design. The skill scaffolds; the human still decides product behavior.
- Generating Python `app.py` from natural language alone. (Possible later, but v1 expects the user — or a separate skill — owns `app.py`.)
- R support. Tracked separately as part of the open question in `DESIGN.md:331-333`.
- Visual design choices beyond the framework binding's defaults. The skill emits structurally correct code; styling polish is downstream.

## Open questions

- **Skill vs. MCP server vs. CLI.** A Claude Skill is the natural starting point (it's how this project already organizes agent tooling), but a CLI or MCP server would let non-Claude tooling participate. Probably ship the skill first; design its prompts/templates so a thin CLI wrapper is feasible later.
- **How do we test the skill itself?** A regression suite of \"prompt → generated app\" pairs, evaluated by running the validation pipeline (above) and a small set of golden snapshots? Worth scoping as a sub-issue.
- **Re-generation conflict policy.** When `app.py` adds an output and the user has manually edited `App.tsx`, what does the skill do? Three-way merge against a generated baseline? Refuse and ask? Mark a region of `App.tsx` as managed?
- **Where do skill-authored conventions live?** Some are skill-internal templates; some (action button pattern, `priority: \"event\"`) belong in `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` so non-skill-driven authors and other agents see them too.
- **Coupling to the framework bindings (#32).** If the user's app needs shadcn, the skill should know to add `@shinyreact/shadcn` to `package.json`, import the components, and wire `extra_deps`. That requires a registry of known bindings the skill can offer — should that registry live in this repo, in each binding repo, or in a shared metadata file?
- **\"Migration\" sub-skill.** Converting an existing traditional Shiny app is meaningfully different from greenfield generation. Sibling skill or one skill with a mode flag?

## Relationship to other issues

- Cross-cuts **#30** (typed Inputs/Outputs codegen) — the skill is a natural caller of typegen on every regeneration.
- Cross-cuts **#31** (enhanced renderers) — the skill must know which renderer methods are available in JSX so it can wire them.
- Cross-cuts **#32** (UI-framework npm bindings) — the skill is how a user picks \"I want shadcn\" or \"I want MUI\" without learning each binding's setup.
- Cross-cuts **#33** (downstream package strategy) — the skill follows the conventions #33 establishes (extra_deps wiring, idempotence pattern, double-load avoidance).
- Cross-cuts **#28** (`@posit/shiny` as npm) — once that lands, the skill's `package.json` template gets cleaner.

## References to existing roadmap notes

- `docs/timeline.md:70` — \"Specific tooling — e.g., a skill, MCP server, or prompt templates that help Claude scaffold shinyreact apps\"
- `docs/timeline.md:124` — \"AI integration … skill/MCP server, API refinement\"
- `DESIGN.md:259-272` — \"AI tooling for generating the client\" + \"Generated client verification\"
- `DESIGN.md:288-290` — \"Migration path for existing Shiny apps\"
- `DESIGN.md:331-333` — R-side variant question
- `DESIGN.md:345` — Next-steps item: \"Invest in AI tooling — build the Claude Skill\"

title: Shiny client runtime as an npm package
description:
From `DESIGN.md` § Shiny client runtime as an npm package:

Today, `shiny.js` (the client runtime that establishes the websocket, manages input/output bindings, etc.) is embedded inside the Python and R packages and injected via HTMLDependency at serve time. It is not available as an npm package. In the SPA-first world, the client needs to explicitly depend on the Shiny runtime — it must appear in `package.json` and be importable by the bundler. This requires publishing `shiny.js` as an npm package (e.g., `@posit/shiny`). This is a significant upstream ask to the Shiny team.

Similarly, the `shiny-react` bridge hooks (currently vendored in this repo) need to be published as `@posit/shiny-react`. The dependency chain becomes:

```
app's package.json
  → @posit/shiny-react (bridge hooks)
    → @posit/shiny (client runtime — websocket, input/output bindings)
    → react, react-dom
```

This eliminates the current fragile pattern of IIFE bundles, `window.shinyreact` globals, and shared React instances to avoid duplicates. With proper npm packages, the bundler handles dependency deduplication natively.

title: Run a third FEATURES.md audit once the tree stack has merged
description:
`FEATURES.md` has had two adversarial audits ([stack #231](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinyreact/pull/229) era). Audit #2 finished at 512/519 leaves confirmed, and the fixes it triggered — #237 through #241 — then changed roughly a third of the tree. That is more churn than either prior audit started from, so the file is due another pass.

Both previous audits found their errors **concentrated in the newest sections**:

- Audit #1's 12 contradictions were nearly all in leaves written in the same session.
- Audit #2's 5 contradictions included leaves that contradicted a test already in the repo (`test-output-ui.R`), a stale Public API claim, and four mis-parented `###` sections.

The sections most rewritten by #237–#241 are exactly the ones with no audit behind them yet:

- **Client registries** — `getReactRegistry()` / `getMessageRegistry()` page-scoping (#228, #229)
- **Wire protocol** — `protocol/surface.json` and the three surface guards (#240)
- **`[js]` Pushed-dependency client** — the `installed` latch and npm-entry install (#239)
- **Client hooks** — `MISSING` cancelling a pending send, the priority-change warning, `useShinyOutputValue` resetting on id change (#241)
- **Page entry points** — per-request mode re-check in `ReactApp`, the `_read_document_cached` mtime gate (#241)

Run `/audit-shinyreact-features`. The skill already builds its inventories first and reports coverage as fractions, so the deliverable is the same as audit #2:

- per-leaf `CONFIRMED <file:line>` / `CONTRADICTED <what the code does>` / `NOT FOUND IN CODE`
- the reverse pass: behavior in the code that no leaf claims

2. **Cross-check the new tests against their leaves in both directions.** #238 and #240 added guards whose whole purpose is to fail when the surface drifts; a leaf claiming a guard exists is worth less than a leaf stating what the guard's failure message tells the reader.

## Not in scope

Stack #244 (#237 → #241) merging. Auditing mid-stack would produce verdicts against code that is about to change.

title: The {{ headContent() }} marker check is not <head>-scoped, in either language
description:
Split out of #223 (item 14) so it can be decided on its own.

## Behavior

`page_react_html()` requires the document to contain a `{{ headContent() }}` marker, and both languages check for it with a plain substring/fixed-string match over the whole file:

- `[py]` `if _HEAD_CONTENT_MARKER not in index_html`
- `[r]` `grepl("{{ headContent() }}", html, fixed = TRUE)`

So a marker in `<body>` — or in a comment, or inside a `<script>` — passes the check, and the dependencies then render **there**, in the body. Meanwhile both error messages assert the marker belongs "inside `<head>`":

> `{path}` must be a complete HTML document containing a `{{ headContent() }}` marker inside `<head>`

The check and the message disagree. A document with the marker in the wrong place is accepted, and the resulting page has shinyreact's script and stylesheet tags in the body — which mostly works (scripts execute, stylesheets apply) but is not what the docs promise, and `<link>` in `<body>` is invalid HTML.

## Why this is not obviously worth fixing

Scoping the check to `<head>` means parsing, or at least locating `<head>`…`</head>` and searching within it. That is more machinery than the current one-liner, and it would **reject** documents that work today — someone deliberately putting the marker mid-document to control script order would break on upgrade. Neither language has a test for the body-marker case, so the blast radius is unknown.

## Options

1. **Soften the messages** to say "containing a `{{ headContent() }}` marker" and drop the `<head>` claim — smallest change, makes the docs true, keeps the permissive behavior. Add a test pinning that a body marker is accepted.
2. **Scope the check to `<head>`** and error otherwise. Truthful and stricter; a breaking change for anyone relying on the current tolerance.
3. **Warn** when the marker is outside `<head>` but proceed. Splits the difference; adds a warning path to maintain in both languages.

My preference is (1): the current behavior is defensible, and the message is the only thing that is actually wrong. If we later want (2), a release with the warning from (3) is the way to get there.

Whichever way, both languages change together, and `FEATURES.md`'s leaf (which documents the mismatch today) gets updated.

title: Python: automatic renderer dep discovery for Core mode / late registrations (port R's flush-diff push)
description:
R now ships zero-config renderer dependency discovery (#203/#146): the `shinyreact.default` input handler installs a per-session `onFlushed` hook (plus a `.shinyreact_init` client ping so zero-input apps are covered), which diffs the session's registered outputs on every flush, extracts each new output's UI/deps via `output_ui()`, and pushes them as a `shinyreact-deps` custom message; the JS bundle loads them and re-runs `bindAll`. Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-r-output-ui-extraction-design.md`.

The same design ports to py-shiny (`input_handlers.add` receives the session; `session.on_flushed(fn, once=False)`), which would give:

- `page_react_html()` (Core mode) the discovery that today only Express's `set_react_page()` has, and
- Express apps dep delivery for outputs registered *after* page load — for **value-based** renderers.

Note this does not touch #160's actual blocker: shinywidgets' `comm_open` custom message racing the dep load. R htmlwidgets have no such side channel, which is why the push works there.

The client half (`js/src/dep-discovery.ts`) is already server-agnostic — the ping goes through `shinyreact.default`, a no-op passthrough in Python today.

title: R: a missing src_dir degrades to "." instead of erroring (page_react)
description:
Split out of #223 (item 12) so it can be decided on its own.

## Behavior

`page_react()` resolves its asset directory with `normalizePath(src_dir, mustWork = FALSE)`, so a missing directory does not error — it silently produces `"."`. Verified live with no `www/` present:

```r
htmltools::renderTags(page_react())
#> <title>.</title>
#> dependency name: "."  → served at /lib/.-0/
```

So an app run from the wrong working directory, or before its client has been built, gets a page titled `.` whose asset dependency points at a directory that does not exist. The `js_file` warning does fire ("JS entry point not found"), which is the only signal — the title and the dependency name are silently wrong.

Python behaves the same way for the title (`base_dir.name` of a nonexistent path), so this is not a parity gap.

## Why it is arguably fine

`mustWork = FALSE` is deliberate: the directory legitimately may not exist yet when the page function runs (a build step creates it), and erroring would break `shiny::runApp()` for an app whose bundle is built on first request. The warning already tells the author the entry point is missing.

## Why it is arguably not

`.` is not a plausible app name or dependency name, so both are certainly wrong rather than merely unhelpful. `/lib/.-0/` in the page source is a confusing thing to hand someone debugging a 404. And nothing tests this path in either language.

## Options

1. **Leave it, add a test** pinning today's behavior so it is at least deliberate.
2. **Improve the fallback** — when the resolved directory does not exist, fall back to a name like `"shinyreact-app"` rather than `.`, keeping the no-error behavior.
3. **Error** when `src_dir` does not exist. Cleanest signal, but breaks the build-on-first-request case above and changes behavior for anyone relying on it.

My preference is (2) with a test: it keeps the permissive resolution that exists for a reason, while removing the nonsense name. Whichever way, `FEATURES.md`'s leaf for this needs updating — it currently documents the `.` degradation as-is.

title: Protocol scope drifted: #221 added two boundary shapes without a version bump
description:
Found while updating `FEATURES.md` for the #221 delta.

All three protocol constants carry the same comment: the wire protocol "covers the shapes that cross the client/server boundary — the `#shinyreact-config` payload itself, the `shinyReactMessage` custom message, and the `shinyreact.default` / `shinyreact.asis` input-handler contract — and only bumps when one of those changes" (`pkg-py/src/shinyreact/_protocol.py`, `pkg-js/src/shiny-react/config.ts`, `pkg-r/R/protocol.R`).

#221 added two more boundary shapes and left `PROTOCOL_VERSION` at `1.0`:

1. the **`shinyreact.init` input-handler name**, plus the `.shinyreact_init` ping id the client sends
2. the **`shinyreact-deps` custom message**, whose payload is a list of `createWebDependency()` results

Both cross the client/server boundary in exactly the sense the comment describes, so the documented scope and the real boundary now disagree.

Whether the version *should* have bumped is a judgement call — arguably not, since both additions are backward compatible in the direction that matters (an older server simply never sends `shinyreact-deps`, and an older client never pings). But two things are worth settling:

- **Update the scope comment in all three languages** so it enumerates what the protocol actually covers. Right now a reader checking "is my change protocol-visible?" gets a list that is missing two entries.
- **Decide the compatibility rule for additive changes** and write it down in `protocol/README.md`: does adding a message type or handler name require a minor bump? If minor bumps are meaningful, note that the client only compares majors, so a minor bump is documentation rather than enforcement.

Related: the audit of `FEATURES.md` flagged "the protocol covers exactly three boundary shapes, and bumps only when one changes" as **UNVERIFIABLE** — a policy with no test behind it. This issue is that abstraction leaking: the policy was already unenforced, and it silently went stale one PR later. A test that fails when a new `addCustomMessageHandler` type or registered handler name appears without a corresponding version change would make the rule real.

title: output_ui()'s no-outputFunc error message is unreachable and its hint is false
description:
Found by the second `FEATURES.md` audit. `pkg-r/R/output-ui.R:33-39` aborts when a render function carries no `outputFunc` attribute, with this hint: > `shinyreact::reactive_output` render functions deliberately have none -- the React client owns their UI. That is not true. `reactive_output()` calls `shiny::createRenderFunction()` without an `outputFunc`, and shiny's `markRenderFunction` substitutes a **placeholder** constructor rather than leaving the attribute unset: ```r rf <- reactive_output({ 1 }) is.null(attr(rf, "outputFunc", exact = TRUE)) #> FALSE as.character(shinyreact:::output_ui_or_null(rf, "x")) #> "
\n  No UI/output function provided for render function.\n
" ``` So: - the abort branch is **unreachable for `reactive_output()`**, the one case its message calls out; - `output_ui_or_null()` does not skip `reactive_output()` outputs — it builds shiny's `
` placeholder and finds zero dependencies in it.

The behavior is harmless (a dep-less UI contributes nothing to the harvest), so this is a correctness-of-documentation issue, not a runtime bug. But the message actively misleads: someone debugging a dependency-discovery problem is told a thing about `reactive_output()` that the code disproves.

Note `pkg-r/tests/testthat/test-output-ui.R:53` — *"output_ui() on reactive_output yields shiny's dep-less placeholder"* — already pins the true behavior, so the test suite and the error message disagree with each other.

## Suggested fix

Either

1. reword the hint to describe what actually happens (shiny substitutes a placeholder; the harvest finds no dependencies), keeping the abort for genuinely attribute-less render functions; or
2. detect the placeholder explicitly in `output_ui_or_null()` and return `NULL`, which would make the harvest skip these outputs as the comment intends — at the cost of depending on a shiny internal detail (the placeholder's identity).

(1) is the smaller and more honest change. Whichever way, `FEATURES.md`'s leaves for `output_ui()` have been corrected to describe the current behavior.

title: npm build omits the pushed-dependency client: no renderer dep discovery for bundler-tier apps
description:
Found by the second `FEATURES.md` audit, verified in the built artifacts.

`installDepDiscovery()` is called from `pkg-js/src/index.ts` (the IIFE entry) but **not** from `pkg-js/src/npm.ts` (the ESM entry that `vite.config.npm.ts` builds).

```
$ grep -c 'shinyreact-deps\|shinyreact_init' pkg-js/dist/shinyreact.js      # IIFE
1  1
$ grep -c 'shinyreact-deps\|shinyreact_init' pkg-js/dist-npm/index.js       # npm
0  0
```

Consequences for an `@posit/shinyreact` consumer:

1. **No `shinyreact-deps` handler.** Dependencies the server pushes are never rendered, and `bindAll` is never re-run, so a `<ShinyOutput>` that mounted before its binding existed stays unbound.
2. **No `.shinyreact_init` ping.** That ping is what bootstraps discovery server-side (`shinyreact.init` → `install_dep_discovery()`), so on an R server discovery is never even installed for the session — the feature is absent end to end, not merely unused on the client.

So the automatic renderer dependency discovery #221 shipped works for the IIFE tier and silently does nothing for the npm tier. A bundler-tier app rendering plotly or a data frame through `<ShinyOutput>` gets a chart that never binds, with no error explaining why.

## Fix

`installDepDiscovery()` in `npm.ts` alongside the existing `requireShinyReactConfigTag()` is the obvious candidate — both are import-time side effects that adapt the client to the server it meets. Worth confirming that is wanted, though: the npm entry is otherwise side-effect-light by design (it exports hooks and does not touch the DOM), and dep discovery adds a custom-message handler plus an input write at import.

If the omission is deliberate, it needs saying out loud — in `protocol/README.md` and in the npm package README — because "same source, both builds speak the same protocol" (`decisions/2026-08-17-js-distribution.md`) currently implies parity that does not hold.

## Test hole this exposes

Nothing asserts which entry installs what. A test over the two built artifacts — or over the two entry modules' side effects — would have caught this, and would catch the next divergence. Related to #201 (SPIKE: how to verify js code).

title: R: no renderer-dependency discovery (Python's set_react_page() has it, R has nothing)
description:
Found while writing the R pass of `FEATURES.md` (behavior tree), sweeping for parity gaps.

## The gap

Traditional Shiny renderers (`@render.data_frame`, `render_plotly`, htmlwidgets) ship `HTMLDependency` objects. For a `ui.tsx`-pattern app to render one inside `ShinyOutput`, those deps have to reach the page.

- **Python:** `set_react_page()` harvests them — top-level renderers *plus* every renderer registered on the session, which covers `@module.server` (#87) — tagifies each `auto_output_ui()` and injects the results into `<head>`. Two Playwright tests pin it (`test_module_renderer_dep_injected`, `test_dynamic_ui_plotly_dep`).
- **R:** nothing. No harvest, no push. An R app using `page_react()` or `page_react_html()` with a traditional renderer inside `ShinyOutput` gets no dependency for it.

`decisions/2026-08-13-r-python-parity.md` records renderer-dependency discovery as an accepted divergence, but the reasoning there is about `set_react_page()` being Express-only. That explains why R has no *`set_react_page()`*; it does not explain why R has no discovery mechanism at all. Python's Core-mode gap is already filed as #220 — this is the R half, which nothing tracks.

## Note: #220's premise appears stale

#220 is titled "port R's flush-diff push" and opens with "R now ships zero-config renderer dependency discovery (#203/#146)": an `onFlushed` hook installed by the `shinyreact.default` input handler, a `.shinyreact_init` client ping, `output_ui()` extraction, and a `shinyreact-deps` custom message.

None of that exists in this repo:

- `grep -rn "shinyreact-deps\|onFlushed\|shinyreact_init"` over `pkg-r/`, `pkg-js/`, `pkg-py/` → no hits.
- `pkg-r/R/input-handler.R` is 53 lines: two pure value transforms, no session hook.
- `js/src/dep-discovery.ts` (referenced by #220) does not exist; the JS lives at `pkg-js/src/`.
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-r-output-ui-extraction-design.md` (referenced by #220) does not exist.
- No commit on any branch mentions the flush-diff push.

So #220 plans to port *from* an implementation that is not in the tree — presumably work that predates the monorepo merge and did not survive it, or landed elsewhere. Worth confirming before #220 is picked up, since its stated approach depends on R code to copy.

## Why it matters

R and Python are supposed to be two implementations of one API (`CLAUDE.md` § Cover both R and Python). This is currently a silent one-sided hole: an R app author following the same pattern as a Python app author gets a chart that never loads its binding, with no error explaining why.

## Suggested resolution

Decide which of these is true and record it:

1. Implement discovery in R (the flush-diff design #220 describes, if it can be recovered from history — or fresh).
2. Declare it a deliberate divergence with a real reason, and add it to `decisions/2026-08-13-r-python-parity.md` explicitly as *no discovery in R*, not just *no `set_react_page()` in R*.

Either way, `FEATURES.md` gets the corresponding leaf. Today it claims `[py]`-only discovery with no `[r]` sibling, which is accurate but reads as an omission rather than a decision.

title: page_react_html() does not auto-discover renderer HTMLDependencies (R counterpart of #87)
description:
Python's `set_react_page()` discovers `HTMLDependency` objects from renderers (including those inside `@module.server`) by harvesting the session's registered outputs at page-generation time — see #87 and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-10-set-react-page-module-dep-discovery-design.md`.

R's `page_react_html()` (pkg-r/R/page.R) is a plain UI function used directly as `shinyApp(ui = page_react_html())`. It does **no** renderer dependency discovery at all — it only reads the HTML file and prepends the shinyreact page dependency. So downstream package dependencies attached by renderers (top-level **or** module) are never injected into `<head>` on the R side.

Decide whether R should mirror Python's session-output harvest (and how, given R Shiny's UI/server split differs from Express's two-pass model), or document the limitation and rely on an explicit dependency mechanism.

Related: #87.
